evidence_text: The Computer History Museum records that Apple II debuted on April 16, 1977 at the first West Coast Computer Faire and was a hit.
decision: Introduce a fully assembled personal computer to a new general audience.
actual_change: Apple debuted the Apple II at the first West Coast Computer Faire.
before_state: Apple was a newly founded personal-computer company.
after_state: Apple had introduced its first mass-market product.
trigger: Demand for accessible personal computing beyond hobbyists.
outcome: The Apple II became Apple’s first mass-market computer.

evidence_text: Microsoft's official history records the April 7, 1975 headline: Altair BASIC is ready and working.
decision: Ship working BASIC software for the Altair microcomputer.
before_state: A new software venture pursuing microcomputer users.
after_state: A working product was available for early microcomputer users.
outcome: Altair BASIC established Microsoft's first product launch.

evidence_text: Microsoft records that IBM introduced its PC with Microsoft's 16-bit operating system, MS-DOS 1.0, on August 12, 1981.
decision: Distribute an operating system through the IBM PC platform.
actual_change: IBM introduced its PC with Microsoft MS-DOS 1.0.
after_state: Microsoft entered the operating-system business through the IBM PC platform.
outcome: MS-DOS established a major operating-system distribution channel.

evidence_text: Microsoft announced retail shipment of Microsoft Windows on November 20, 1985.
decision: Launch Microsoft Windows as a graphical operating environment.
actual_change: Microsoft shipped Windows to retail dealers and distributors.
before_state: Microsoft's operating-system offering centered on MS-DOS.
after_state: Microsoft added a graphical operating environment to its product line.
outcome: Windows began its commercial product lifecycle.

source_title: Here’s How a Four-Page Contract Started The Walt Disney Company
evidence_text: The Walt Disney Company states it officially began on October 16, 1923 when Walt Disney signed a contract to produce and distribute the Alice Comedies.
decision: Secure a distribution contract for the Alice Comedies.
actual_change: Walt Disney signed the contract to produce and distribute the Alice Comedies.
before_state: Walt Disney had moved to Hollywood after earlier studios failed.
after_state: The new studio had a distributor and a first production commitment.
trigger: A distributor needed new animated content.
outcome: The contract established the studio that became The Walt Disney Company.
